arxiv-2203-03569.title: Texture-induced spin-orbit coupling and Skyrmion-electron bound states in a Néel antiferromagnet
arxiv-2203-03569.creator: N. Davier, R. Ramazashvili
arxiv-2203-03569.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by N. Davier, R. Ramazashvili. We derive effective-mass electron Hamiltonian for a Néel antiferromagnet in the presence of a smooth texture of the staggered magnetization. For certain locations of electron band extrema, the texture produces a peculiar and anomalously strong spin-orbit coupling of the scale ℏ ​ v / L \hbar v/L , with v v the Fermi velocity and L L the characteristic length scale of the texture.

arxiv-2301-12818.title: Private, Anonymous, Collateralizable Commitments vs. MEV (Extended Version)
arxiv-2301-12818.creator: Conor McMenamin, Vanesa Daza, Xavier Salleras
arxiv-2301-12818.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce the private, anonymous, collateralizable commitments (PACCs) framework. PACCs allow any smart contract wallet holder to collateralize a claim, request, or commitment in general, in a private and anonymous manner. PACCs can prove arbitrarily much or little about the wallet generating the commitment, and/or the transaction which is being committed.

arxiv-2502-00917.title: Rigidity and Toeplitz systems
arxiv-2502-00917.creator: Henk Bruin, Olena Karpel, Piotr Oprocha, Silvia Radinger
arxiv-2502-00917.description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to study measure-theoretical rigidity and partial rigidity for classes of Cantor dynamical systems including Toeplitz systems and enumeration systems. We use Bratteli diagrams to control invariant measures that are produced in our constructions. This leads to systems with desired properties.

arxiv-2502-08311.title: INFERENCE IN DYNAMIC MODELS FOR PANEL DATA USING THE MOVING BLOCK BOOTSTRAP
arxiv-2502-08311.creator: Ayden Higgins, Koen Jochmans
arxiv-2502-08311.description: Abstract Inference in linear panel data models is complicated by the presence of fixed effects when (some of) the regressors are not strictly exogenous. Under asymptotics where the number of cross-sectional observations and time periods grow at the same rate, the within-group estimator is consistent but its limit distribution features a bias term.

arxiv-2504-08973.title: Observational strategies for ultrahigh-energy neutrinos: the importance of deep sensitivity for detection and astronomy
arxiv-2504-08973.creator: Kumiko Kotera, Mainak Mukhopadhyay, Rafael Alves Batista, Derek Fox, Olivier Martineau-Huynh, Kohta Murase, Stephanie Wissel, and Andrew Zeolla
arxiv-2504-08973.description: Abstract Detecting ultrahigh-energy neutrinos can take two complementary approaches with different trade-offs. 1) Wide and shallow: aim for the largest effective volume, and to be cost-effective, go for wide field-of-view but at the cost of a shallow instantaneous sensitivity – this is less complex conceptually, and has strong discovery potential for serendipitous events.

pmc-11342170.title: Protocol for calculating binding free energy of RNA:RNA interactions through molecular dynamics simulations using adaptive biasing force technique
pmc-11342170.creator: Takeru Kameda, Daniel K Saha, Sourav Ray, Yuichi Togashi, Katsura Asano
pmc-11342170.description: SummaryThe adaptive biasing force (ABF) technique allows sampling to proceed in a flat free energy surface when performing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. pmc-12568579.creator: Saci-Elodie Marty, Linda Yip, Fangyuan Wang, Manoj Kumar, C. Garrison Fathman
pmc-12568579.description: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) play a central role in immune homeostasis and the preservation of immunological self-tolerance. Treg activity depends on prolonged IL-2 receptor (IL-2R) signaling, and impairment or loss of this function has been linked to the development of autoimmune diseases.

pmc-12574448.title: Ferroptosis-Related Gene CRYAB in Asthma: Bioinformatics Identification and Experimental Validation
pmc-12574448.creator: Jiahui Lei, Yingjie Guo, Fan Gao, He Zhu, Jinxin Ma, Limin Zhao
pmc-12574448.description: BackgroundFerroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of asthma. This study aimed to identify and validate ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) associated with asthma through bioinformatics analysis, clinical samples, and experimental validation, thus providing new insights for treatment.MethodsTranscriptome data from induced sputum samples of asthma patients were obtained from the GEO database.

pmc-13060748.title: Cultural Adaptation of a Digital Mobile App for Bipolar Disorder (PolarUs): Protocol for a Qualitative Co-Design Study
pmc-13060748.creator: Leena W Chau, Jill K Murphy, Emma Morton, Martin D Provencher, Delphine Raucher-Chene, Steven J Barnes, Erin E Michalak
pmc-13060748.description: BackgroundBipolar disorder (BD) affects approximately 40 million people worldwide and is a chronic, potentially disabling mood disorder. pmc-13291812.title: GroupStruct2: A User-Friendly Graphical User Interface for Statistical and Visual Support in Species Diagnosis
pmc-13291812.creator: Kin Onn Chan, L Lee Grismer
pmc-13291812.description: Statistically defensible species diagnoses are essential for producing robust taxonomies, which underpin much of biological research. Yet, most species descriptions remain largely descriptive, often lack rigorous statistical validation, and suffer from confounding factors stemming from sampling bias, geographic variation, and intraspecific diversity.

pmc-13477407.title: Comparison of Vascular Aging Models on the Basis of Different Vascular Indicators for Cardiovascular Events Prediction: A Chinese Community‐Based Cohort Study
pmc-13477407.creator: Haotai Xie, Fangfang Fan, Jia Jia, Jianping Li, Yanjun Gong, Yan Zhang
pmc-13477407.description: BackgroundVascular aging (VA) is a promising concept for cardiovascular risk assessment, but the optimal vascular indicator for vascular age calculation remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare VA indices on the basis of different vascular indicators for predicting cardiovascular events.MethodsThis prospective study included 3561 participants from a Chinese community‐based cohort.

pmc-13559361.title: Research trends and cellular targets of NF-κB pathway in acute lung injury [2005–2024]: a combined bibliometric analysis and systematic review
pmc-13559361.creator: Jie Shen, Xia Shen, Fan Ping, Bingyue Yang
pmc-13559361.description: BackgroundThe nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway is a key regulator of inflammation and immune responses in acute lung injury (ALI). Despite significant progress in elucidating the molecular and cellular mechanisms of the NF-κB pathway in ALI, current research is scattered across different disciplines, experimental models, and cell types.

pmc-13578382.title: Early-onset adenocarcinomas of the distal esophagus, gastroesophageal junction, and stomach: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 45 studies

pmc-13578382.description: BackgroundThe incidence of adenocarcinomas of the distal esophagus, gastroesophageal junction (GEJ), and stomach diagnosed before age 50 years is increasing and early-onset disease may have a distinct phenotype. A comprehensive synthesis of clinicopathological and molecular differences between early-onset and average-onset disease remains lacking.
